comparison: Both evaluate c-Fos immunohistochemical findings (C5, C6, C44-C52, C68, C102). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical analyses and specificity controls. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, acknowledging the correlation but expressing concern about pathway complexity and requesting more detailed analysis of which hippocampal neurons and layers showed c-Fos changes.

Both evaluate behavioral findings across T-maze tasks (C3, C4, C29-C33, C36, C38-C42, C63-C66). OpenEval finds clear dissociation between lesion groups with adequate statistical support (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers also find results SUPPORTED, describing them as 'interesting and important' with 'remarkable' maze rotation effects, though requesting more discussion about the surprising lack of PCFx effects.

Both evaluate geometric discrimination control task (C91-C94). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting this provides critical control for non-specific lesion effects and supports specificity of allocentric spatial working memory deficits. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, implicitly accepting intact performance as evidence for deficit specificity without raising concerns.

Both address histological lesion verification (C22-C27). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with converging evidence from quantitative measurements, comparisons, and appropriate interpretation of white matter vs. neuronal loss. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, requesting more detailed anatomical analyses, improved photomicrographs, neuronal measurements, and c-Fos analysis in MB subdivisions.

Both evaluate the major theoretical conclusion about mammillary body function (C7, C79, C99, C100). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting the dissociation provides strong support for reinterpretation and is logically consistent with experimental findings. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, finding results 'interesting and important' but requesting more explicit discussion about PCFx role to clarify contrast with memory systems dissociation.

Minimal overlap (C20 only - acetylcholinesterase staining). OpenEval R1 addresses comprehensive histological validation (C17-C27) rated SUPPORTED. Peer R4 addresses PCFx lesion validation (C13, C20, C67) also rated SUPPORTED, noting 'very precise lesions' without concerns about specificity or completeness.

Minimal overlap (C13 only - anatomical rationale). OpenEval R7 addresses anatomical/functional rationale for lesion approach (C13-C16, C58-C62) rated SUPPORTED. Peer R4 addresses PCFx lesion validation including anatomical precision, both finding evidence adequate.

OpenEval evaluated historical context and field characterization (C1, C2, C8-C12, C53-C56) as SUPPORTED, noting accurate characterization based on appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background/contextual claims.

OpenEval evaluated contextualization of c-Fos findings within diencephalic amnesia literature (C57, C69-C73) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate caution about functional significance. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these literature contextualization claims.

OpenEval evaluated discussion of surprising lack of PCFx effects (C74-C78) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate speculation about task demands and redundancy. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers did request more discussion of PCFx role in their R1 and R6 evaluations.

OpenEval evaluated mechanistic discussion about mammillothalamic tract effects (C80-C89) as SUPPORTED, noting well-reasoned inferences based on electrophysiological and anatomical evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these mechanistic interpretation claims.

OpenEval evaluated clinical relevance and translational potential discussion (C95-C98) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate acknowledgment of limited human data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these translational claims.

OpenEval evaluated methodological validity claims (C28, C37, C43, C104) as SUPPORTED, noting critical behavioral controls and appropriate c-Fos timing. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific methodological details.
